en.title: Shortest Path Through a Required Waypoint
en.description:
You are given a weighted directed graph with n nodes, where an edge [u,v,w] is a one-way edge from u to v with non-negative weight. Output the shortest distance from start to target, and the shortest distance of a route that must pass through waypoint; output -1 for whichever does not exist. A route through waypoint may revisit nodes and edges.

This site's additions: nodes in the input are numbered from 0; a route is a walk, so nodes may be revisited on the segment to waypoint or the segment leaving waypoint; distances use 64-bit integers. The original snapshot's code in three languages also added every edge in reverse, which contradicts its second example; based on the directed version with the same function signature, examples and constraints, this site corrects it to one-way edges.
en.input: The first line contains n m; each of the next m lines contains u v w; the last line contains start target waypoint.
en.output: Output two integers: the shortest distance and the shortest distance through waypoint; if there is no solution, the corresponding value is -1.
en.explanation: Run Dijkstra from start and from waypoint on the original directed graph. The first value is the distance from start to target; the second is the distance from start to waypoint plus the distance from waypoint to target. Because edge weights are non-negative, the optimal constrained route can be formed by joining two shortest paths; the route may revisit nodes.
hints: Edges are one-way; do not automatically add reverse edges.
A route through waypoint may revisit vertices.
The largest answer may exceed the 32-bit integer range, so use 64-bit distances.
